---
title: "Error rates under two denominators"
subtitle: "2.14 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section II and slides 22 and 25–26"
description: "Relation between expected errors per possible pair and expected errors per stated pair."
---

Both error rates divide the same expected wrong count $E$ by different pair totals: KRW's discordance rate $\mathrm{DR} = E/M$ uses all $M$ pairs, while $E/N$ uses the $N$ stated pairs.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **τ .25.** Stating 14 of 15 pairs (share .933) gives DR .0238 and E/N .0255; the two rates stay close when almost all pairs are stated.
- **KRW setting.** KRW's race card states 1,324 of 4,656 pairs (share .284), shrinking E/N .136 to DR .0387 (KRW risk −.0227, postrank risk .1818).
- **All pairs stated.** Stating all 15 pairs makes both denominators equal, so DR and E/N both equal .0480 while the archived card stays fixed.

```{=html}
<details>
<summary>Rounding and archived card probabilities</summary>
<p>For positive <em>N</em>, DR = (<em>N</em>/<em>M</em>) &times; <em>E</em>/<em>N</em>; rounded displays use an approximation sign when multiplying rounded shares does not reproduce the rounded product. Both rates are expectations over pairs, whereas the chance of at least one error depends on the joint distribution. KRW's archived card statistics and the evaluation on released pair probabilities agree at the displayed digits; we evaluate the archived grade assignments under postrank's loss.</p>
</details>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
ev <- postrank_evaluate(c(A=1,B=2,C=3,D=3,E=4,F=5),pr_tutorial$one,weights=c(score_A=1),tau=.25)
ev[c("N","M","E_over_M","E_over_N")]
```
:::
